analysis.title: Nvidia CEO Change Looking Increasingly Likely; Key Topics of Investor Discussions
key_insights: Wells Fargo says new details make it increasingly likely the NVDA board will be forced to make a CEO change. This is a flash comment dated 11/12/2026, and the rating stays Overweight with a $300 price target.

News flow cited: WSJ reports the board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang as CEO after a NYT report alleging an extramarital relationship with a VP who reports directly to him. Bloomberg then reported NVDA hired an outside firm to identify CEO candidates and may name an interim CEO.

Wells Fargo expects NVDA to most likely name an interim CEO during an external and internal search. It views CFO Colette Kress as the most likely interim, with Ian Buck (VP of Hyperscale & HPC) gaining visibility.

The bank is reluctant to view a CEO change as a near-term clearing event for the shares. It sees little to no risk of demand destruction and remains confident in out-year estimates, citing NVDA's leadership position and supply chain capabilities.

On long-term revenue CAGR and market share without Huang, Wells Fargo says NVDA's supply chain scale, supplier investments and relationships, and efficiency and throughput gains remain the key competitive differentiators. Huang helped cultivate them, but the bank thinks they can be sustained.
On valuation, NVDA shares trade at a discount to the SOX. Wells Fargo argues sustained above-average growth and margins can justify a premium valuation even without Huang.

Management structure is an open question. The CEO's roughly 60 direct reports is likely not sustainable or repeatable under a new CEO and could slow coordination on the product roadmap and time to market. The bank's view is unknown but likely to change.
Many of NVDA's strategic investments in the AI ecosystem were driven personally by Huang, so the pace or trajectory of that investment could change. Wells Fargo's view is unknown.

Government scrutiny or action related to sales to Megaspeed could remain a lingering question. Wells Fargo calls it a likely drawn-out risk and says to watch for details from an 11/18 closed-door briefing.

Valuation: the $300 price target is about 15x P/E on C2028E. The bank argues NVDA should at least trade in line with the SOX P/E, and says peak-share concerns have compressed the multiple. At $173.73 the target implies 72.7% upside.

Key person risk around founder and long-time CEO Jensen Huang is listed among the risks to the price target and rating, alongside competition, new-market development and delays from third-party process technology.

market_movers.rationale: Little to no risk of demand destruction from a CEO change, and confidence in out-year estimates given NVDA's leadership position and supply chain capabilities.

sector_views.rationale: NVDA is described as one of the most attractive secular growth stories in large-cap semis, supported by CUDA differentiation and data center, HPC and AI opportunities.

tension_points.bull_case: Wells Fargo sees little to no risk of demand destruction and remains confident in out-year estimates. It cites NVDA's supply chain scale, supplier relationships and efficiency gains, and says sustained above-average growth and margins can justify a premium valuation.
tension_points.bear_case: Investor questions include a lower long-term revenue CAGR and market share, a lower long-term multiple in line with the SOX, slower roadmap coordination if the roughly 60-direct-report style does not carry over, and a change in the pace of AI ecosystem investments Huang drove personally.
